reconciliation_rules.title: Fenced negative controls
reconciliation_rules.rule: A future-domain prohibition is an active Phase 1 negative control introduced at M0R when the scanner first runs. It is not a positive deferred-domain obligation. Revalidate at the first affected implementation surface and at M6.

reconciliation_rules.title: Atomic split threshold
reconciliation_rules.rule: Split an original requirement when clauses have different introducing gates, materially different owners/evidence, or combine positive runtime behavior with a separately testable negative phase-boundary control. Do not split merely because one sentence contains multiple assertions at the same gate.

reconciliation_rules.title: Mechanism versus realization
reconciliation_rules.rule: Introduce a reusable mechanism at the earliest gate where it is executable. Revalidate the concrete later surfaces it governs. Move the whole clause to M6 only when no meaningful earlier behavior can be executed.

reconciliation_rules.title: Production-artifact claims
reconciliation_rules.rule: Claims that explicitly require the built production image, production roles, destructive restore or complete deployable surface are introduced at M6 unless the requirement contains an independently executable earlier clause.

reconciliation_rules.title: M5 boundary
reconciliation_rules.rule: M5a owns focused outlet-node services, local persistence, synchronization and print resilience. M5b owns same-QR DNS/TLS resolution and local authority continuity. Split clauses that cross this boundary.

reconciliation_rules.title: Evidence links
reconciliation_rules.rule: Use a golden journey only when it directly exercises the clause. Otherwise use an explicit engineering test. Revalidation must name the later artifact or behavior, not merely the milestone.

active_requirements.title: Same-QR routing and node-key custody
active_requirements.required_behavior: The same opaque table QR uses a per-outlet public hostname. Public DNS routes to cloud and outlet split-horizon DNS routes to the LAN node. The node generates and retains its private key, submits only a CSR, and receives the public-CA certificate chain from central DNS-01 automation; the private key is never exported.

Public DNS routes normally to cloud; outlet split-horizon DNS resolves that hostname to the LAN node. A public-CA per-outlet certificate is issued through central DNS-01 automation and securely provisioned to the node. The lifecycle is measurable: renewal begins at 30 days before expiry, retries on a bounded backoff, raises an operator alert at 14 days and a critical alert at 7 days, records installation evidence (served-certificate fingerprint and expiry verified from the LAN) before the renewal is considered complete, keeps per-outlet private keys generated and held on the node under documented custody, supports compromise revocation and re-issuance, and on failed renewal fails safe to the cloud-served journey with translated staff guidance rather than a browser warning. Shared cross-outlet wildcard private keys, raw local IP URLs, self-signed warnings and manual browser bypass are prohibited.

active_requirements.title: Monotonic authority replacement and fencing
